name: OH-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Michael Rulli running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger raised only about $1,200 with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Rulli at roughly 97% to win
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Rulli's incumbency and roughly $1.1 million raised against a challenger with about $1,200, and markets pricing him near 97% all point the same way, so the forecast stays at a Safe R margin near -17.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending in the district would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 6th District is a heavily Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+17, and first-term incumbent Michael Rulli is running for reelection. He has raised over $1.1 million and holds roughly $270,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Elizabeth Kirtley has reported only about $1,200 raised and no outside support on either side. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets give Rulli about a 97% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the lopsided money advantage. The forecast expects Rulli to win by roughly 17 points, with the main source of uncertainty being the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
